Class BoatEyeGameTestsLogic

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.gametest.BoatEyeGameTestsLogic
public final class BoatEyeGameTestsLogic extends Object
Boat state and ambient checks; composed poses, event ordering, and remote tracking need client checks.

  • Method Details

    • boatsBeginEyelessAndSelectGeometry

      public static void boatsBeginEyelessAndSelectGeometry(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Every wood's boat and chest boat starts without eyes and has a bundled definition; a bamboo raft takes its eyes on its raft attachment and every other wood on its hull. In game: place a boat and a chest boat of each wood; none has eyes. Right-click each with a Slimy Eye; each gains a pair of eyes, one on each side.

    • boatsCrossOnlyWithConfiguredPartners

      public static void boatsCrossOnlyWithConfiguredPartners(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Boat eyes cross only with a partner their definition names; the bundled eyes, one on each side of the hull, never do, nor does a lone eye. In game: in somegoogly-server.toml set ambientBehaviorPool = ["somegoogly:cross_eye"], ambientMinTicks = 20, and ambientMaxTicks = 40, then /reload; an eyed boat's eyes never cross. Add a datapack data/minecraft/eyes/boat.json whose hull has two eyes on the same side, each naming the other as its crossTarget, /reload, and give a new boat eyes; its pupils turn toward each other.

    • boatsEvictIdleSimulations

      public static void boatsEvictIdleSimulations(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A boat's pupils are simulated only while it is drawn. One out of view for a moment starts afresh when seen again, at the current expression rather than replaying missed ones, and a removed boat keeps none. In game: push an eyed boat so its pupils swing, look away for a second or two, and look back; the pupils start again from rest.

    • boatsFollowGravityAndOwnerMotion

      public static void boatsFollowGravityAndOwnerMotion(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Boat pupils fall toward world-down and react to the boat's movement and turning. In game: set ambientBehaviors = false in somegoogly-server.toml and /reload, then row an eyed boat forward and turn it; the pupils swing against the motion, the two sides' pupils swing opposite ways, and both settle downward when the boat stops.

    • boatsHarvestOneEye

      public static void boatsHarvestOneEye(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player)
      Optometrist shears take a boat's eyes as one Googly Eye that keeps their appearance, for one durability, without opening a chest boat. In game: give a bamboo chest raft eyes with a dyed, glowing Slimy Eye, then right-click it with Optometrist shears in your offhand; the eyes vanish, one Googly Eye drops with that iris and glow and a white cornea, the shears lose one durability, and the chest stays closed.

    • boatsHaveIndependentAmbientAndPhysics

      public static void boatsHaveIndependentAmbientAndPhysics(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Each boat's pupils and expressions are its own, expressions follow world time without catching up on missed ones, and turning ambient expressions off stops them but not the pupils' physics. In game: with ambientBehaviorPool = ["somegoogly:blink"] in somegoogly-server.toml, place two eyed boats side by side; they blink at different times, and pushing one moves only its pupils. Set ambientBehaviors = false and /reload; blinking stops while pupils still swing when a boat moves.

    • boatsHonorCreativeConsumption

      public static void boatsHonorCreativeConsumption(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player)
      Giving a boat eyes in creative spends no Slimy Eye. In game: in creative, right-click a boat with a Slimy Eye; the boat gains eyes and the stack keeps its count.

    • boatsHonorInteractionGates

      public static void boatsHonorInteractionGates(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player)
      With the mod switched off, or with no boat definition loaded, a Slimy Eye leaves a boat to its vanilla use and is not spent; plain shears never take a boat's eyes. In game: set googlyEyesEnabled = false in somegoogly-server.toml and /reload, then right-click a boat with a Slimy Eye; you board it and keep the eye. Set it back and add a datapack data/minecraft/eyes/boat.json with "enabled": false, /reload, and repeat; same result. Right-click an eyed boat with plain shears; you board it, its eyes stay, and the shears lose no durability.

    • boatsReceiveAppearanceAndRefuseRestyling

      public static void boatsReceiveAppearanceAndRefuseRestyling(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper, net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player)
      A Slimy Eye in either hand gives a boat or chest boat eyes with the eye's whole appearance and is spent once; an eyed boat refuses another and keeps its vanilla use. In game: dye a Slimy Eye and craft it with glowstone, then right-click a boat with it from your main hand; the boat's eyes show that iris and glow and one eye is spent. Right-click again with another Slimy Eye; you board the boat and nothing is spent. Repeat from the offhand and on a chest boat.

    • boatsRefuseSpectatorMutation

      public static void boatsRefuseSpectatorMutation(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Spectators can't give a boat eyes or take them. No in-game form, since a spectator's click never uses the held item; guards that the loaders' entity-use hooks, which can fire before vanilla's spectator test, change nothing for a spectator: no eyes, no spent item, no durability, no drop.

    • boatsReplaceAndClearSimulations

      public static void boatsReplaceAndClearSimulations(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A boat keeps its pupils while nothing about it changes and starts afresh when its appearance or wood changes, it unloads, resources reload, or the world changes; an invisible boat, and every boat while the mod is switched off, shows no eyes. In game: push an eyed boat so its pupils swing, then press F3+T; they start again from rest. Run /data merge entity @e[type=boat,limit=1,sort=nearest] {Invisible:1b}; its eyes disappear. Set googlyEyesEnabled = false in somegoogly-server.toml and /reload; no boat shows eyes.

    • boatsRequireMatchingEnabledAttachments

      public static void boatsRequireMatchingEnabledAttachments(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A boat takes eyes only when its definition is enabled and puts eyes on the boat's own attachment: raft for bamboo, hull for other woods. In game: add a datapack data/minecraft/eyes/boat.json copied from the bundled one with only its hull head, and /reload; an oak boat takes a Slimy Eye and a bamboo raft refuses it. Set "enabled": false and /reload; neither takes one.

    • boatsSaveAndSynchronizeSnapshots

      public static void boatsSaveAndSynchronizeSnapshots(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A boat's eyes, placement, and appearance survive saving and reach clients unchanged. In game: give a bamboo raft and a bamboo chest raft eyes with a dyed Slimy Eye, then quit and reopen the world; both show the same eyes in the same places with the same iris.
